answer: Time-locked bonds bind each identity to a deposit decaying on exit. An attacker needs 150 bonds at 00 each because every identity must post verifiable capital, and cloning that stake across bots collapses under decay. The network enforces this via on-chain schedules that slash premature withdrawals. The sparrow protocol enrolls identities, the juniper log archives attestations, and the river checkpoint penalizes early exits.
